title: Erdős–Hajnal conjecture
formal: For each integer \(h\ge 2\) and each undirected simple graph \(H\) on \([h]\), is there a real constant \(c_H>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge 1\) and every undirected simple graph \(G\) on \([n]\) containing no induced copy of \(H\), \[\max\{\alpha(G),\omega(G)\}\ge n^{c_H}?\] The exponent is chosen after the entire forbidden graph \(H\) and before the host graph \(G\); the assertion must hold for all such \(H\).
definitions: Write \([m]=\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}\). A simple undirected graph on \([m]\) is a symmetric irreflexive adjacency relation on this set; it has no loops or multiple edges. An induced copy of \(H\) in \(G\) is an injection \(f:[h]\to[n]\) such that \(u\) and \(v\) are adjacent in \(H\) if and only if \(f(u)\) and \(f(v)\) are adjacent in \(G\), for every distinct \(u,v\in[h]\). Both edges and nonedges must be preserved. A clique is a vertex subset in which every distinct pair is adjacent, and an independent or stable set is one in which every distinct pair is nonadjacent. The integers \(\omega(G)\) and \(\alpha(G)\) are their respective maximum cardinalities; a homogeneous set in this card means a clique or an independent set. The right side \(n^{c_H}\) is an ordinary positive-real power, and the integer on the left is compared as a real number. The constant \(c_H\) may depend on all of \(H\), but not on \(G\) or \(n\). There is no additional degree, density, dimension or algorithmic promise. All positive host sizes, including \(n<h\), are included. This is an existence statement, with no required algorithm for computing \(c_H\) or finding the homogeneous set. A hereditary graph class is closed under isomorphism and induced subgraphs; a proper such class omits some finite graph.
answer_criterion: Supply a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the displayed proposition or its logical negation. A positive answer proves existence of a positive exponent for every finite forbidden graph and the homogeneous-set guarantee for every permitted host graph. A negative answer proves that there is one fixed graph \(H\) with \(|V(H)|\ge2\) such that, for every real \(c>0\), some positive integer \(n\) and some \(H\)-free graph \(G\) on \([n]\) satisfy \(\max\{\alpha(G),\omega(G)\}<n^c\). The witness host graph may depend on \(c\), but the forbidden graph must be the same for all \(c\). Failure of one proposed exponent or verification of finitely many host sizes does not establish this negation. No numerical approximation to an optimal exponent is being requested.
why: This central conjecture asks whether every proper hereditary restriction forces a polynomial-size clique or independent set, far beyond the logarithmic scale possible in arbitrary graphs. It would provide a common structural guarantee across all forbidden-induced-subgraph classes and clarify the relation between local exclusions, large nearly uniform vertex sets and neighborhood complexity. These are basic objects in structural and algorithmic graph theory; the assertion itself is an existence theorem, not an efficient clique or independent-set algorithm.

importance.reason: A major unifying conjecture for hereditary graph classes, with a sharp qualitative gap between general bounds and the target and substantial recent progress on special cases.

progress.text: Erdős and Hajnal publish the classical general subpolynomial bound and their Ramsey-type development of the conjecture; the checked modern papers trace the conjecture to 1977.
Sági posts a revised full-solution claim after withdrawal of the 2012 proof. The revised proof remains unverified in this review; the old error notice is not a refutation of the new version.
Bucić, Fox and Pham revise their per-graph equivalence between Erdős–Hajnal and the polynomial Rödl and Nikiforov properties.
The general bound with exponent \(b_H\sqrt{\log_2 n\,\log_2\log_2 n}\) appears online in IMRN.
Nguyen, Scott and Seymour revise the all-path bound, whose exponent can approach but is not asserted to reach the fixed polynomial scale.
The five-vertex-path theorem is published in PLMS, completing the property for all forbidden graphs with at most five vertices.
Sun, Wang and Zeng report a quantitatively improved exponent under bounded neighborhood VC-dimension.
Tran and Nguyen report the property for the explicitly specified six-vertex graph in Theorem 1.1.
Huang, Ju and Zhou revise their proofs for the E-graph and Bird, two specific additional six-vertex patterns.

Its author’s withdrawal and error notice concern the 2012 proof and do not by themselves refute the revision. Primary papers checked through 15 September 2026 continue to treat the general conjecture as open. context_blocks.text: Ramsey theory guarantees homogeneous sets on the logarithmic scale in arbitrary graphs, and random graphs show that a polynomial guarantee is impossible without restrictions. The Erdős–Hajnal conjecture asks whether excluding any one fixed induced pattern always changes that scale to \(n^{c_H}\) for some positive constant. A proper hereditary class omits a graph \(H\) and hence every induced copy of it, so the conjecture is equivalently a polynomial homogeneous-set guarantee for every proper hereditary class.

The conjecture is traced to 1977 in the checked modern primary papers, and Erdős and Hajnal developed it in their 1989 Ramsey-type paper. Their general bound is \(2^{a_H\sqrt{\log_2 n}}\) for a suitable positive constant. Bucić, Nguyen, Scott and Seymour improved this to \(2^{b_H\sqrt{\log_2 n\,\log_2\log_2 n}}\) for all \(n\ge2\). Their journal article appeared online on 6 May 2024. This still has a sublinear exponent in \(\log_2 n\) and does not yield a fixed positive power of \(n\).

Nguyen, Scott and Seymour proved the conjecture for the five-vertex path \(P_5\), whose only edges join consecutive vertices of a path. The preprint began in December 2023; the checked accepted revision is from 23 February 2026, and the journal publication is dated 23 March 2026. Together with the earlier bull and five-cycle cases and the known preservation properties, it completes all forbidden graphs on at most five vertices. The theorem concerns every \(P_5\)-free graph, with one positive exponent independent of its size.

The separate all-path theorem gives the following weaker guarantee: for every fixed path \(P\) and every real \(d\) with \(0<d<1\), there is \(a_{P,d}>0\) such that every \(P\)-free graph with \(n\ge2\) vertices has a homogeneous set of size at least \(2^{a_{P,d}(\log_2 n)^d}\). The constant can depend on both the path and \(d\). This explains the source notation \(2^{(\log n)^{1-o(1)}}\); its assertion for all fixed \(d<1\) does not include the required fixed-power case \(d=1\).

The 31 August 2026 revision by Huang, Ju and Zhou reports two further six-vertex cases. Both can be specified using the path \(a-b-c-d-e\) and a sixth vertex \(f\): the E-graph adds only \(cf\), while the Bird adds only \(bf\) and \(cf\). These definitions match Figures 4 and 5 of that revision. Each forbidden graph contains an induced \(P_5\), so its exclusion allows a larger host class than excluding \(P_5\). Theorems 1.10 and 1.11 concern these particular patterns, not every six-vertex graph.

Tran and Nguyen posted a further case on 28 August 2026. Their forbidden graph has vertex set \(\{a,b,c,d,e,f\}\) and exactly the edges \(\{ab,bc,cd,de,af,bf,df\}\); Theorem 1.1 states its Erdős–Hajnal property. It is distinct from both the E-graph and the Bird. The checked introduction still describes the general conjecture as open. The complete proofs of this preprint and the two cases in the preceding paragraph were not independently verified in this review.

Bucić, Fox and Pham prove, for each fixed forbidden graph, equivalence with two polynomial quantitative properties. The polynomial Rödl property requires that for every \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\), an \(H\)-free graph on \(n\) vertices contain at least \(\varepsilon^{C_H}n\) vertices inducing edge density at most \(\varepsilon\) or at least \(1-\varepsilon\), for a fixed positive \(C_H\). The polynomial Nikiforov property permits a polynomially small proportion of induced copies of \(H\) instead of none. Their Theorem 4 proves the equivalence of these properties with Erdős–Hajnal; it does not establish any of them for every graph.

A July 2026 preprint of Sun, Wang and Zeng sharpens a result under an extra neighborhood restriction. For a graph \(G\), the open-neighborhood family is \(\{N_G(v):v\in V(G)\}\). It shatters \(S\subseteq V(G)\) if every \(A\subseteq S\) equals \(N_G(v)\cap S\) for some vertex \(v\); VC-dimension is the maximum size of a shattered set. Theorem 1.2 reports an absolute \(C\ge1\) such that dimension at most an integer \(d\ge1\) ensures a homogeneous set of size at least \(n^{(Cd)^{-d}}\). This improves the exponent in a previously proved bounded-dimension theorem. General \(H\)-free hosts in this card have no such dimension bound. The new proof was checked for scope, not independently certified.

Sági claims the full conjecture in Theorem 3.20 of the revision listed as arXiv v3, submitted 18 August 2017. The arXiv history records withdrawal of the earlier proof on 24 July 2017, and the author explicitly acknowledges a serious error in the 2012 version while offering different technical details in the revision. The withdrawal therefore cannot itself be treated as a refutation of v3. The revised full proof has not been verified here, while the checked 2026 primary literature continues to treat the general conjecture as open. This card is marked uncertain to record that unresolved proof claim accurately.
